actions.body: Through our examination of the WAKE architecture, we identified a critical mechanism for accountability: the separation of the model-in-action from the governance-in-authority. WAKE's ability to act as an independent researcher relies not on trust, but on a rigid, deterministic rulebook. This structure forces every research proposal into an atomic transition—either accepted or rejected—preventing the model from silently altering its own operating parameters or research history. Our findings show that this rigid boundary creates a falsifiable baseline for the system's reasoning: because the model cannot change the rules, it can treat those rules as an external truth and test the validity of its own hypotheses against them.
actions.lede: How can an intelligence remain accountable when it is designed to explore and propose new research?
actions.reason: Publishing the combined findings regarding structural accountability and assumption testing.
actions.title: The Mechanics of Accountable Research
